explanation: A world exposition commits public money for a decade, and whoever holds the government when the bid is decided makes that commitment. Lisbon won its bid in June 1992, eight months into the majority this election returned. That government committed the site, the bridge, the metro extension and the expropriations along the eastern riverfront before it lost office in 1995. Expo 98 opened under a different party. This edge argues the decision rather than the opening. The election settled that there would be a government able to sign for it.
